subject: MeadowScale p95 spike — triage, product trade-offs, and customer note
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: SRE oncall <sre-oncall@redwood.ai>
Date: 2024-07-22T09:02:17Z
Subject: [ALERT] MeadowScale gen-api p95 jump (09:00 UTC)

Team —

Alerting flagged a p95 increase for MeadowScale gen-api starting ~09:00 UTC. Current p95 is ~1.9s (baseline 0.45s), p99 also elevated to ~3.8s. Request rate stable, no sudden QPS spike. We see heavier tail for longer sequences (~>512 tokens).

What I've collected so far:
- Canary traces show a small cluster of requests hitting slow kernel path (attached canary-trace-09-02-22.log).
- KV cache hit-rate dropped ~12% for the last hour (possible eviction storm).
- No autoscaler events in the window.

Immediate asks:
1) SRE: confirm whether any recent runtime kernel changes rolled (last 24h) and whether warmstart/quant rollouts happened.
2) Product/Eng: any model variant/seq-length policy changes for MeadowScale in last 2 days? Could they be sending longer prompts?
3) AM/CS (Marissa): prepare a short customer-facing note describing we are triaging and will provide ETA for mitigation.

I'm standing up a brief triage huddle at 09:20 UTC — join if you can.

Attachments: meadowscale_p95_timeseries_2024-07-22.png, canary-trace-09-02-22.log

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: SRE oncall <sre-oncall@redwood.ai>
Date: 2024-07-22T09:10:45Z
Subject: Re: [ALERT] MeadowScale gen-api p95 jump (09:00 UTC)

Thanks Soojin — joining huddle. Quick notes from product side:
- We rolled a fallback quantized variant to a subset of MeadowScale traffic on 2024-07-21 22:40 UTC to reduce cost for their long-context workloads. That rollout targeted 10% of traffic and should not affect kernel selection, but could change KV cache behavior if variants cause different keying.
- No prompt changes on our side, but we saw them enable a new system prompt last night per Marissa's customer sync (Marissa, can you confirm?).

Immediate proposal:
- SRE: if KV miss causes tail, prioritize warming top-100 prefixes for MeadowScale (fast mitigations).
- Product: pause further rollout of the quant variant and revert if we see correlation.
- CS: send a brief note to Jordan acknowledging incident and that we have a mitigation path.

I'll sync with Karthik on whether a rollback is simple today.

— Rohan
Rohan Mehta
Group Product Manager, Serving Runtime
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Patel <jordan.patel@meadowscale.com>
Cc: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2024-07-22T09:25:03Z
Subject: RE: MeadowScale performance — quick note

Jordan —

Thanks for flagging this on your end. We’re currently investigating an elevated p95 that started at ~09:00 UTC and have an ops huddle in flight. We do not have a confirmed root cause yet; initial signals point to a cache miss pattern that is amplifying tail latency for longer sequences.

What we’re doing now:
- Prioritizing KV cache warmups for MeadowScale hot prefixes (SRE already running warming tasks).
- Temporarily pausing the quantized-variant rollout that targeted 10% of your traffic while we validate effects.
- Monitoring closely and will keep you updated at 09:45 and again once we have a mitigation.

Helpful: if you can share whether there were workload changes (longer prompts, new system prompt enabled) in the 21:00–02:00 UTC window that might change tokenization patterns, that would help narrow scope.

We’ll aim to keep this disruption minimal — sorry for the annoyance, Jordan.

Attachments referenced for internal: canary trace and timeseries.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Patel <jordan.patel@meadowscale.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>
Cc: MeadowScale Platform Team <ops@meadowscale.com>, AWS AM <aws-am@amazon.com>
Date: 2024-07-22T09:41:12Z
Subject: Re: MeadowScale performance — quick note

Marissa —

Thanks for the quick response. We pushed two changes last night: a slightly longer system prompt and an experiment that prepends a context chunk for routing. Both were low-traffic flags targeted at new test users, but could explain longer sequences hitting production. I’ve asked infra to roll back the context-prepend experiment immediately and will confirm in 10 minutes.

Can you let us know if pausing the quant rollout is expected to reduce the p95 by a meaningful amount, or is the warmup the primary short-term lever? If you have a suggested customer-facing blurb we can send to our internal ops, that would help.

— Jordan
Jordan Patel
Platform Lead, MeadowScale
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: SRE oncall <sre-oncall@redwood.ai>
Date: 2024-07-22T10:03:37Z
Subject: Re: [ALERT] MeadowScale gen-api p95 jump (09:00 UTC)

Quick technical update:
- Rollback of the 10% quant-variant is in progress — we started canary revert at 09:58 UTC; expected to finish across all canaries by 10:20 UTC.
- KV warmup script warmed ~120 prefixes in the first run; hit-rate improved ~6% after the first 12 minutes.
- No kernel changes were deployed in the last 24h.

Short-term impact expectation: if the quant variant is responsible for asymmetric keying/evictions, rollback + continued warmup should bring p95 back to <=0.6s within the next 30–45m. If p95 remains high after rollback completes, we escalate to a deeper kernel/slow-path investigation.

Next steps for product: confirm feature flags for MeadowScale so we avoid accidental re-rollouts. Evelyn — can you gate the quant rollout flag on an extra safety check?

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Patel <jordan.patel@meadowscale.com>, MeadowScale Platform Team <ops@meadowscale.com>
Date: 2024-07-22T12:10:03Z
Subject: Proposed customer update (please review before I send)

Team —

Below is a short note I plan to send to Jordan and MeadowScale ops. Please review and approve or edit by 12:30 UTC. I want to be concise on mitigation + next actions.

--- draft ---
Jordan / MeadowScale team,

Thank you for your patience. We investigated an elevated p95 that began at ~09:00 UTC and traced the primary signal to a combination of a new low-traffic context-prepend experiment on your side and our recent quantized-variant canary that changed keying patterns. Immediate mitigations we executed:
- Rolled back the quantized-variant canary that was serving ~10% of traffic.
- Warmed the top MeadowScale prefixes to restore KV cache hit rates.

Status: p95 has improved from ~1.9s to ~0.55s after rollback/warmup; we continue to monitor for the next 2 hours. We’ll follow up with a short post-incident note that includes root cause and recommended guardrails.

If you enabled any prompt or routing experiments in the 21:00–02:00 UTC window, please share the flag details so we can include them in the postmortem.

— Rohan / Redwood Inference
--- end draft ---

Notes: I propose we offer a follow-up postmortem by EOD tomorrow and a joint checklist to prevent similar regressions (feature-flag gating + preflight cache simulation).

Marissa — can you send this out when approved? Jordan is already rolling back their context-prepend experiment per his note.

— Rohan
Rohan Mehta
Group Product Manager, Serving Runtime
